selected.rationale: Losing the Redis cart edge kills all Basket.API reads/writes; the API has no local fallback, so cart and checkout become unavailable.
A delay on the synchronous cart call directly stalls the user-facing checkout flow; without a strict per-request timeout it can consume connection/thread pools and propagate latency.
The UserCheckoutAccepted event is lost on this edge, so Ordering.API never creates the order; this exposes the missing outbox/broker-confirm recovery behavior.
Lost integration events from Ordering.API prevent stock/payment/status workflows from advancing; order state silently stalls without retry or dead-letter.
Catalog DB latency hangs catalog reads for both webapp and mobile BFF, and EF retries amplify the delay rather than providing a timeout, causing unbounded latency.
A delay in order placement RPC can exhaust webapp retries/HttpClient timeouts and produce user-visible failures or duplicate orders, showing missing timeout/idempotency controls.
When the order processor loses its RabbitMQ edge, it cannot consume or publish order state changes, so the entire order lifecycle stalls.
Delayed payment events back up in the queue and defer payment status, exposing the absence of bounded latency or priority handling on the payment path.
Identity API latency makes login/registration calls hang for all users; without a separate timeout the webapp's retry policy can turn a small delay into a long outage.
Order persistence fails on DB loss, so submitted orders are lost and the integration event log cannot advance, leaving order state inconsistent.
